title: A Forgotten Particle May Explain Why the Universe Exists
summary:
Scientists have proposed a surprising new explanation for why the universe exists at all, and it centers on a mysterious particle that physicists have largely overlooked for decades. Researchers from the University of Southampton and the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur say this forgotten particle may have helped matter survive after the Big Bang.

The puzzle is simple to state and hard to solve. Scientists believe matter and antimatter were made in nearly equal amounts in the early universe. When opposites meet, they destroy each other, so exactly equal amounts would have left almost nothing to build stars, planets or life.

The team's answer involves a heavier relative of the neutrino, an extremely lightweight particle that rarely interacts with ordinary matter. This type, called a 'decoupled' heavy neutrino, was long dismissed as too weakly connected to matter. But the researchers calculated that it decays incredibly slowly, so it lived long enough to temporarily dominate the universe's energy as the cosmos cooled after the Big Bang.

That brief dominance could have changed the temperature at which fundamental particles, like electrons and other leptons, interacted with their antiparticles with the help of the Higgs boson. That temperature acts like a switch, said study author Dr. Rishav Roshan of the University of Southampton, shaping how the small surplus of matter over antimatter built up. "The fact that we are here at all proves that an asymmetry between matter and antimatter occurred," he said.

The findings were published in Physical Review Letters, a journal of the American Physical Society. The idea is a proposed explanation, not proof, but it shows how something long considered insignificant may have helped decide why the universe contains matter at all.
why_it_matters: If a particle everyone ignored helped decide whether anything exists at all, it shows how the smallest, quietest things can shape the biggest questions.
